title: Completed local normal form for invertible Kummer monoid extensions
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $R,Q$ fine saturated monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and $h:R\to Q$ an injective homomorphism such that every $q\in Q$ has a positive multiple in $h(R)$. Assume that $h^{\rm gp}$ is injective with finite cokernel annihilated by a positive integer $N$ invertible in $A$. Let $\alpha:R\to(A,\cdot)$ be a homomorphism, put $G=\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)$ and $S=R_G/G^{\rm gp}$, where $R_G=\{r-g:r\in R,g\in G\}\subset R^{\rm gp}$. Suppose a homomorphism $a:S\to(A,\cdot)$ and a character $\epsilon:R^{\rm gp}\to A^\times$ have been chosen such that $\alpha(r)=\epsilon(r)a(\bar r)$ for every $r\in R_G$, where $\bar r$ denotes its image in $S$ and $\alpha$ is extended to $R_G$ by inverting its units. Assume the maximal-ideal completion $\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], compatibly with the monomials $a(u)$, has one of the following presentations for some finite $n\ge0$: (a) $k[[S]][[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$, where $k=A/\mathfrak m$ is a coefficient field; (b) $V[[S]][[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(\theta)$, where $V$ is a Cohen ring with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta\equiv p\pmod{(S\setminus\{0\},t_1,\ldots,t_n)}$, with $p$ the uniformizer of $V$. Here formal monoid rings are completions of $E[S][t]$ at $(\mathfrak m_E,S\setminus\{0\},t)$, and monoid rings have basis $[u]$ and multiplication $[u][v]=[u+v]$.
Put $C=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $\mathfrak q$ be any prime of $C$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$, put $B=C_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $F=\{q\in Q:[q]\in B^\times\}$, $T=Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$ with $Q_F=\{q-f:q\in Q,f\in F\}$, and $J=([q]:q\in Q\setminus F)B$. Then there is a nonzero complete regular Noetherian local ring $D$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and a continuous isomorphism identifying the indicated ideals as follows:
$$ (\widehat B,J\widehat B)\cong (D[[T]],([v]:v\in T\setminus\{0\}))\quad\text{in case (a)},$$
$$ (\widehat B,J\widehat B)\cong (D[[T]]/(\eta),([v]:v\in T\setminus\{0\}))\quad\text{in case (b)},$$
where $\widehat B$ is the maximal-ideal completion, $D[[T]]$ is the completion of $D[T]$ at $(\mathfrak m_D,T\setminus\{0\})$, and the reduction $\overline\eta\in D=D[[T]]/(T\setminus\{0\})$ belongs to $\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2$.

source.place: Expose VI 2.3, printed p.73, completed equal- and mixed-characteristic Kummer chart formulas; arbitrary unit faces and chart twists made explicit as in the existing formal-monoid-extension model.

proof.text: Choose generators $q_i$ of $Q$ and integers $d_i>0$ with $d_iq_i=h(r_i)$. The tensor ring $C$ is generated over $A$ by their monomials, each satisfying $Z_i^{d_i}=\alpha(r_i)$; the finitely many products with exponents less than $d_i$ span $C$ as an $A$-module. Thus $C$ is finite type and Noetherian by the cited permanence result. Apply the finite-completion-factor statement with $R=A$, $S'=S=C$ and $g=1$: it identifies $\widehat B$ with the selected idempotent factor of $\widehat A\otimes_A C$. All monomials and their generated ideals are preserved. We can therefore perform the calculation over the displayed complete presentation of $\widehat A$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text: The local map $A\to B$ reflects units, so $G,F$ are faces and $h^{-1}F=G$. Face sharpening gives sharp fs monoids $S,T$ with finite free group completions. For $f\in F$, choose $r\in R^{\rm gp}$ with $h(r)=Nf$, and use the Kummer condition to write $df=h(r_0)$ with $r_0\in R$, $d>0$. Injectivity gives $dr=Nr_0\in R$, so saturation gives $r\in R$. Since $[h(r)]=[f]^N$ is a unit in $B$, locality gives $r\in G$. Thus $NF^{\rm gp}\subset h(G^{\rm gp})$, and $h_U:G^{\rm gp}\hookrightarrow F^{\rm gp}$ has finite cokernel killed by $N$. The induced $\beta:S\to T$ sends only $0$ to $0$: if $h(r-g)$ is a unit in $Q_F$, then $h(r)$ belongs to $F$ and $r\in G$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text: Put $U=G^{\rm gp}$ and $V=F^{\rm gp}$. Split each quotient group sequence using lifts of a basis of the free groups $S^{\rm gp}$ and $T^{\rm gp}$. These group sections restrict to monoid sections: a lift of a monoid class differs from any representative by a unit, which can be added or subtracted in the localized monoid. Thus $R_G\cong U\oplus S$ and $Q_F\cong V\oplus T$. In these coordinates $h(u,s)=(h_U(u)+c(s),\beta(s))$, with $c:S^{\rm gp}\to V$. Write $\alpha(u,s)=\rho(u)e(s)a(s)$; here $\rho=\alpha|_U$ and $e(s)=\epsilon(j_S(s))$ are unit characters, because $\alpha=\epsilon a$ and the section $j_S$ is additive. No extension of $\epsilon$ to $Q^{\rm gp}$ is needed, and neither $U$ nor $V$ is assumed torsion free.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text: With $A_0=\widehat A$, impose the unit relations first: $A_1=A_0\otimes_{\mathbf Z[U]}\mathbf Z[V]$, using $\rho:U\to A_0^\times$. The tame group-algebra lemma applies to the injective map $h_U$ with finite cokernel killed by the invertible $N$, even if its unit groups have torsion. It gives complete local finite etale factors $K$. The split monoid presentation gives the remaining relations $[c(s)]Y^{\beta(s)}=e(s)X^s$. After completing at the chosen prime, exactly one factor $K$ occurs: modulo the nonzero $T$-monomials all nonzero $S$-monomials vanish by these relations, so the residue prime is precisely a closed-point factor of $A_1$. In particular its residue field equals $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text: Put $E=k[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ in case (a), and $E=V[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ in case (b). The power-series/Cohen statement makes $E$ nonzero complete regular Noetherian local. Iterating the defining inverse limits of the formal monoid presentations gives $A_0=E[[S]]/(f)$, where $f=0$ in case (a) and $f=\theta$ in case (b). Apply the finite-etale formal-monoid coefficient-lift lemma to the selected local finite etale $A_0$-algebra $K$. It supplies a nonzero complete regular Noetherian local finite etale $E$-algebra $D$ with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $K\cong D[[S]]/(f)$. In mixed characteristic it also preserves every nonzero cotangent class from $E$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text:
Under this isomorphism the unit character $e(s)[c(s)]^{-1}$ in $K$ lifts to a character $v:S^{\rm gp}\to D[[S]]^\times$: choose arbitrary unit lifts of its values on a basis of the free group $S^{\rm gp}$ and extend multiplicatively; reduction recovers the given character. This needs no root extraction. The completed presentation of the selected factor is therefore
$$D[[S\oplus T]]/(f,\ Y^{\beta(s)}-v(s)X^s\ (s\in S)).$$
To check this presentation, start with $R_G=U\oplus S$ and $Q_F=V\oplus T$, take the balanced tensor quotient on their monomial generators, impose the unit relations to obtain $K$, and then complete. Completion of the quotient is the quotient of the completion by the generated relations by the cited theorem. All these rings are Noetherian: the monoids are finitely generated and finite-type permanence and completion preserve Noetherianity. Changing unit lifts changes the displayed relations only by multiples of $f$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text: Apply implicit monoid elimination with coefficient ring $D$, monoids $S,T$, the map $\beta$ (whose inverse image of $0$ is $\{0\}$), and character $u(s)=v(s)^{-1}$. The relations are $X^s-u(s)Y^{\beta(s)}$. The lemma identifies their quotient with $D[[T]]$, sends each nonzero $S$-monomial into the nonzero-$T$ ideal, and is the identity on $D$ on the stratum. Thus in equal characteristic the required ring is $D[[T]]$. In mixed characteristic the additional relation becomes the image $\eta$ of $\theta$, so the required ring is $D[[T]]/(\eta)$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text: In mixed characteristic reduce the elimination substitution modulo the nonzero $T$-monomials. Every nonzero $S$-monomial is zero and the coefficients are fixed, so $\overline\eta$ is the image of $\theta_0=\theta|_{S=0}\in E$. The hypothesis says $\theta_0\equiv p$ modulo $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. In the regular power-series ring $E=V[[t]]$, its linear term in the parameter $p$ has coefficient $1$, so $\theta_0\in\mathfrak m_E\setminus\mathfrak m_E^2$, including $n=0$. The coefficient-lift lemma preserves this class in $D$, proving $\overline\eta\in\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

proof.text:
Finally $Q_F=V\oplus T$ identifies a monomial from $Q\setminus F$ with a unit times $Y^t$ for $t
e0$. Conversely any $t
e0$ has a representative $q-f$ with $q
otin F$, so $Y^t$ is a unit times the image of $[q]$. Hence the two generated ideals coincide, before and after completion and after the mixed quotient. The elimination isomorphism fixes $Y$-monomials, so it identifies $J\widehat B$ with the indicated nonzero-$T$ ideal. Each isomorphism was formed on completed local rings and respects their ideals of definition, hence is continuous. The ring $D$ and its residue field are those of Step 5. This proves the asserted pairs in both cases, also for $T=\{0\}$.

source.place: ILO VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73; explicit algebraic details of the completed chart calculation.

Step 2: face sharpening; N-torsion of V/h(U) by Kummer, injectivity and saturation; beta^-1(0)=0. Step 3: section into R_G. Step 4: tame group algebra; a single factor K whose residue field is kappa(q). Steps 5-6: the coefficient lift, unit lifts on a basis, presentation D[[S+T]]/(f, Y^beta(s) - v(s)X^s). Step 7: elimination with u=v^-1. Step 8: theta_0 = p mod (t) is not in m_E^2, and the lift preserves this. Step 9: ideal J. All 3 new nodes are true. Tame group algebra: cyclic filtration, Z^d - a with d invertible, so etale; tested on L=0, M=Z/2. Coefficient lift: henselian E (Stacks 09ZL), 07NF regularity, 031B completeness, m_D=nD with an injective cotangent map. Elimination: a contractive multiplicative substitution gives a retraction, and complete Nakayama gives surjectivity.
